claims.text: Our phone-audio recordings measured an uncalibrated relative mean level of -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound from Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green across 6 runs.
Our phone-audio recordings measured an uncalibrated relative mean level of -19.42 dBFS(A) eastbound from Bethnal Green to Mile End across 6 runs.
Across 11 within-trip paired runs, Liverpool Street-Bethnal Green was on average 0.54 dB higher in uncalibrated relative audio level than Bethnal Green-Mile End.
Indicative sound level meter measurements over one whole eastbound trip between Liverpool Street and Mile End recorded an LAeq of 91.9 dB(A) including platform and dwell time.

These indicative app readings cannot be compared like-for-like with TfL's figures because TfL measurements were taken in train operator cabs, while our app measurements were taken in passenger saloons, included platform and dwell times, and were on single trips.
TfL stated in December 2022 that rail grinding to remove corrugation must be repeated at regular intervals, usually 6 months to a year, to maintain effectiveness.

claims.text: A secondary press report citing JRPass claimed Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green registered 92.8 decibels, but this secondary figure is not TfL primary data.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels
Daniel de Nieuwe, Head of Product from JRPass said:

claims.text: In July 2026, Assembly Member Elly Baker highlighted at Mayor's Question Time that TfL Government Relations turned down requests for specific noise data citing constrained resources.

citations.quote:
Last week, I received an email, not from Andy Lord - I did not get a letter back from Andy Lord, despite the
fact we put a lot of effort into that letter, making sure it was really comprehensive - just an email from TfL's
Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data. It contained the reassuring phrase,
"We are fully committed to tackling Tube noise, but – as you have said – resources remain constrained".

asks.request: Request the complete log of completed rail grinding and track reconditioning works on the Central line between Liverpool Street and Mile End (specifying date, track direction, and exact chainage) from May 2022 to date.
asks.why: Public disclosures confirm grinding took place up to May 2022 (claim-01) and reconditioning was scheduled for 2023/24 (claim-02), but the public record lacks verification of whether works occurred or were repeated within the recommended 6 to 12 month interval (claim-11).

asks.request: Request all bi-monthly in-cab and saloon noise monitoring surveys conducted by TfL on the Central line between Liverpool Street and Mile End from July 2024 to date.
asks.why: TfL conducts noise readings bi-monthly (FOI-1231-2425), but the latest disclosed official section-level in-cab dataset is from June 2024 showing levels up to 87 dB LAeq (claim-03, claim-04); current official levels remain undisclosed to Assembly Members (claim-13).

asks.request: Clarify the provenance and methodology of the 92.8 dB figure reported for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green in January 2026 media reports attributing data to TfL via JRPass.
asks.why: The 92.8 dB figure appears in media reporting as TfL data but is unverified against primary FOI releases, creating confusion about whether it represents peak saloon exposure or cab monitoring (claim-12).
